newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - Portugal's jobs data good news for EMU hopes.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Portugal's jobs data good news for EMU hopes.

text.p: Portugal on Friday announced a sharp drop in second quarter unemployment, which economists say boosts its chances of meeting a key budget deficit goal and qualifying to join the European single currency from the start.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) announced a plunge in unemployment to 6.5 percent of the workforce, or 299,900 people, in the second quarter, from 7.3 percent in the first quarter and 7.2 percent in the second quarter of 1996.
INE said the main reason for the reduced unemployment rate was an increase in jobs in agriculture and construction.
"This drop in unemployment is clearly associated with a greater-than-expected growth in the economy," said Rui Martins dos Santos, Banco Portugues de Investimento chief economist.

Keith Edmonds, economist with IBJ International in London, told Reuters: "More jobs will raise government tax revenues, and the government will have to pay out less in unemployment benefit, which is good news for the 1997 budget deficit target."

Edmonds estimated that Portugal would turn in a budget deficit of slightly above the target of three percent of GDP at the end of the year, taking into account some inaccuracies in official forecasts of tax revenues and government spending.

Martins dos Santos was optimistic that Portugal would meet the budget deficit goal and join Economic and Monetary Union at its launch in 1999, as he expected politicians to adopt a flexible approach to Maastricht convergence criteria.

He said France's admission that it will not cut its deficit this year to three percent of GDP and Germany's struggle to control its public finances would encourage policy makers to focus more on longer term trends in economic activity.
The economist said Portugal suffered less acutely from unemployment than many of its European partners because it had a more flexible labour market and less generous social benefits.
He said the unemployment rate could fall further in the third quarter as summer tourism and preparations for the Expo 1998 Lisbon World Fair generated jobs.

Employment Minister Maria Joao Rodrigues has said she expected jobs to be created in services -- for example, in health, education and culture -- as well as automotive, electronics and paper industries.
She has said the Socialist government aimed to boost job creation by pursuing sound macroeconomic policies that reduced inflation and interest rates to stimulate conditions for investment.
Economists say the Bank of Portugal has room to cut interest rates further this year.
The government offers incentive programmes to industry to encourage businesses to recruit and train well-qualified people as well as programmes to encourage people to set up companies.
